line_status.note: Under the yod of both the first word and the second word the print shows two vertically stacked dots (shewa), not a single horizontal stroke (patach); Reading A's יַגֶּה / וַיַּגֶּה is wrong. The rest (וַיְיַגֶּה, יָגָה I.) is identical in both and matches the print.

Under the yod in both יֶגֶל and וַיֶּגֶל the print shows a three-dot segol cluster, not a qamets stroke; the apocopated Hiphil of גלה is indeed יֶגֶל/וַיֶּגֶל. Reading B matches; Reading A's qamets under yod is wrong.
The second letter of both forms is printed as a dalet (square shoulder, top bar projecting right of the stem), not a resh; this agrees with the root דָּאָה "to fly" named on the same line.

Under the כּ of the headword the print shows two side-by-side dots (tsere, ֵ), not a qamets stroke; so יִדַּכֵּא (Reading B), the regular Hithpael vocalisation. The rest of the line (fut. Hithp. from r. דָּכָא.) matches both readings.

The root's first letter is a dalet (flat top, protruding right shoulder, no left leg), identical to the דָּמַם printed two lines below and consistent with the context (Niphal forms of דמם); it is not a he.

Second letter of both Hebrew forms is ה (open gap at top-left of the left stroke), not ד, matching the root הָמַם cited on the lines above and below; the yod carries tsere, not hireq. Reading B is correct.

First word is הָמַם (he, matching "r. הָמַם" in line 1), not דָּמַם — no dagesh in the first letter. The last word is printed חֳיְהָ with an accent stroke above the ח (hateph under ח, sheva under י, qamets under ה); Reading A's חִיָּה is wrong and Reading B omits the accent.

Third letter is dalet, not resh: the printed letter has a squared top-right corner with the bar overhanging the downstroke (resh in this font is rounded). Context confirms: the entry (יְהוֹדֶה, Hiph. fut. of ידה) is a Chaldaism for יוֹדֶה.

Printed left-to-right order: the short three-letter form יְהִי (yod-sheva, he-hiriq, yod) stands at the left margin, followed by the four-letter וַיְהִי (vav-patah). Reading A swaps them; Reading B matches the print, including all vowel points and הָיָה with two qamats.

The headword's yod carries a shewa (two vertically stacked dots), not a patach (single horizontal stroke), so יְהֵל (B) matches the print; the rest of the line is identical in both readings and in the image.
The last root's first letter has the ת foot (תָּלַל with dagesh, not הָלַל), and the headword shows qamets under ה, tsere + dagesh in ל and shureq (יְהָתֵלּוּ, Job 13:9 form), not יְהַתְלוּ.
Second Hebrew word is printed יְאָכְלוּ: sheva under yod (not tsere as in A), qamets under aleph and no dagesh in kaf (not qibbuts/dagesh as in B).
The vowel under the resh of the first word is a three-dot segol (same as the parenthetical יוֹרֶה and the MT of Prov. 11:25), not a two-dot tsere; Reading B's יוֹרֵא is wrong.
Both yods carry a patach (single horizontal stroke), not tsere; compare the clearly two-dotted יֵז at the start of line 3, which is the Kal form contrasted with this Hiph. patach form.

The second form after "and" has a single dot (hireq, יִז), not a patach bar — the patach form יַז is the Hiph. one on the line above, whereas this Kal line gives tsere/hireq (וַיֵּז Is. 63:3, וַיִּז 2 K. 9:33). The two vav-conversive forms are printed tsere first, then hireq, matching the order of the bare forms; Reading B inverts them and misreads the vowel.

First word has qamets (not segol) under yod and plain shewa under zayin with no dagesh, as in A; but the second word's mem carries a dagesh (יָזֹמּוּ, the uncontracted geminate form), as in B. Each reading is right on one word and wrong on the other.

Under the yod of the first word and under the aleph of the second a single dot (hiriq) is printed, not patah; and under the het of אִחֵל two dots (tsere) are printed, not patah. Reading B matches the printed vowels (Piel אִחֵל, with יִחַל the shortened form).

Both words carry a single dot (ḥireq) under the yod, not ṣere/shewa; the first word's lamed has a visible dagesh (the "Dag. forte euphon." the next line refers to), and the second word's ḥet has ḥaṭeph pataḥ, not pataḥ. Reading B matches on all points.

Under the yod the print shows a single dot (hireq), not the T-shaped qamets of Reading A — consistent with the Piel lemma יִחַל referred to by the euphonic dagesh remark (Lgb. 85). B's double space after "euphon." is just the wider inter-sentence gap in the print; collapsed to a single space here.

Decisive: under the yod of the second word the mark is a vertical two-dot shva (יְ), not a single-dot hireq; and the first word's yod carries a horizontal two-dot tsere (יֵ) with hataf-patah under the chet, not segol/hataf-segol. Reading A matches the print.
First word: the print has segol under yod and ḥaṭeph‑segol under ḥeth (יֶחֱמַתְנִי), not shva/segol/shva as in A; the second word is identically read by both and matches the print.

Last word is printed אֶחֱרוּ: segol under א and ḥaṭef segol (shewa + three dots) under ח, not ḥaṭef pataḥ + qameṣ (A) or + pataḥ (B). It is the anomalous Piel præt. of Judg. 5:28 cited elsewhere in the lexicon as the parallel to יִחֲמַתְנִי.

First word is printed יָחְנְךָ (qamets under yod, shewa under ḥet) as in A; the second word is printed with dagesh forte in the nun, יְחָנְּךָ, as in B. A drops the dagesh, B mis-points the first word, so neither is exact.

First letter is clearly ח (open at the top-left, no foot like ת) with a qamets beneath, not תּ with tsere/dagesh; the middle letter is a short yod with qamets, and the final ה also carries qamets. Reading A misreads ח as ת and invents a tsere/dagesh; Reading B matches the print.

Under the yod in line 3 a single horizontal stroke (patach) is printed, contrasting visibly with the two-dot tsere under the yod of יֵט / וַיֵּט in line 4 (the Kal form). Hiph. apocopated יַט with patach is also the expected form. The rest of the line (comma after headword, final period after נָטָה) is identical in both readings.
Under the yod the print shows two vertical dots (shewa), not a qamets; under the dalet a qamets (horizontal stroke with tail), not a patach. No point under the ayin. This matches Reading B exactly.
Headword begins yod+sheva, yod+tsere (no vav, no patah, no dagesh) and ends plene ־ִיב, not ־ֶב; third item is יֵיטִיב, matching the parallel יְיֵלִיל/יֵילִיל line below. Reading B matches exactly.

No vav is printed at the start of either the first or the third word: the first word is four letters (yod-yod-lamed-yod-lamed, sheva under the first yod, tsere under the second) and the third is יֵילִיל with tsere under the initial yod, exactly paralleling line 2 (יְיֵטִיב … יֵיטִיב). Reading A's וַ prefixes and הֵ in the third word are not on the page.

The yod carries a sheva (two vertical dots) and the first lamed a tsere (two horizontal dots), not qamets/patach as in A; the form is יְלֵל, so Reading B is correct (ignoring its extra spacing after "wail.").

Printed left-to-right order: the shorter 3-letter form יִיף (no vav) stands at the far left of the line, and the longer vav-consecutive form וַיִּיף (patah under vav, dagesh + hiriq in yod) comes second, immediately before "fut." — the same short-then-long pattern as the next line (יַךְ, וַיַּךְ). Reading A reverses them. Points on יָפָה (qamets, qamets) and the rest match both readings.
The leftmost (first) item on the printed line is the two-letter form יַךְ; the three-letter form with vav, וַיַּךְ, comes second — same order as the preceding Kal line. Reading A reverses the order.

The printed word is defective: kaf carries qubbuts (three dots below) with no vav between kaf and nun — the glyph is clearly shorter than the plene יְכוֹנְנֵהוּ on the next line, and matches MT Job 31:15 יְכֻנֶנּוּ. Reading B's shureq-vav is not printed.

Both second and third forms end in holem-vav מוֹ (dot above the vav is printed; the following lines confirm "מוּ is written for מוֹ"), not shureq as in A; and the second form is יְכַסִּימוֹ with hireq-yod, not B's יְכַסְיֻמוֹ. Only the first word has shureq מוּ.

In the second word the kaf carries a patach (horizontal stroke), not a sheva, and the tav has a dagesh dot before the shureq: יֻכַּתּוּ. The sheva form יֻכְּתוּ appears only in line 4 ("and this for"), which Reading A has conflated with line 2.

Decisive point is the last Hebrew word: under the kaf the print shows a single horizontal stroke (patach), not the two vertical dots of a shewa, and the dot sits inside the tav (dagesh), not the kaf — matching Reading B's יוּכַתּוּ and the parallel forms יֻכַּתּוּ / יְכַתּוּ on the adjacent lines. Everything else (order of items, plene vav in both יוּ- forms, pointing of כָּתַת, "§ 66. 5.") is identical in A and B and matches the print.

All three Hebrew words carry qibbuts (three slanting dots) under the yod, not shewa as in Reading A; the third word has shewa under kaf and dagesh in tav (יֻכְתּוּ, the regular Hophal), not hireq under kaf. Reading B matches the print.

Under the yod of the second word the print shows a single T-shaped qamets, not the two stacked dots of a shewa; the regular Hiph. fut. of an ʿayin-vav root (יָלִיזוּ) confirms qamets. Everything else (patach + dagesh in the first word, לוּז) is as both readings have it.
First word starts with yod (no vav); second word is plene וַיַּלִּינוּ with yod and dagesh in lamed, not defective וַיַּלֹּנוּ with holem as in Reading A.
Under the yod a single dot (hireq), not two (tsere); under the mem a vertical two-dot shewa, not a qamets. Reading A matches the print (the unsyncopated form יִמְרַר underlying יֵמַר).
